summary: reassign overwrites the donor tag's concept_id, destroying its provenance
description:
The `reassign` branch of `applyTagAction` runs three writes against the donor
tag, and the middle one looks purely destructive:

    stmts.deleteEdge.run(tag.chunk_id, `concept.${tag.concept_id}`, 'EXPRESSES');
    stmts.updateStagedTagStatus.run('reassigned', q.reviewer, nowIso(), tag.id);
    stmts.updateStagedTagConcept.run(q.reassign_to, tag.id);   // <-- this one
    stmts.insertReassignedTag.run(tag.chunk_id, q.reassign_to, ...);

`updateStagedTagConcept` is `UPDATE staged_tags SET concept_id=? WHERE id=?`
(db.ts:147). After it runs, the donor row claims it was a tag for the *target*
concept — but the newly inserted row already records the target, with
justification `Reassigned from ${tag.concept_id}`. So the target is stored
twice and the concept the model actually proposed is stored nowhere.

## Why it matters

The donor row is the only record that the tagger proposed X on that chunk. Lose
it and the over-generation statistics silently lose a data point, and
`status='reassigned'` rows can no longer answer "what did the model get wrong
here" — the question node 11 review exists to accumulate an answer to.

Concretely, from the yoga-sutras pass: five donors were `paradox_as_teaching`
(four) and `gnosis_direct_knowledge` (one), chosen *because* those were
over-applications worth recording. Applying the queue erases exactly that.

## Suspected fix

Drop the `updateStagedTagConcept` call. The donor keeps its original
`concept_id` with `status='reassigned'`, the new row carries the target, and
the audit trail reads correctly in both directions.

## Do not fix blind — check these first

1. Does anything read `staged_tags.concept_id` for rows with
   `status='reassigned'` and depend on it naming the *target*? Check the review
   UI's history/queue views and any reporting queries.
2. Existing `reassigned` rows in guru.db already have overwritten concept_ids.
   The original values are unrecoverable, so a fix is forward-only — decide
   whether those rows need a marker distinguishing them from correct ones.
3. Confirm no unique-index interaction: the donor is already out of
   `idx_staged_tags_provenance_unique` (partial on `status='pending'`) by the
   time this runs, so leaving concept_id alone cannot reintroduce a collision.

Raised while converting rejects to reassigns for silent-omission repair
(docs/ingest/decisions/yoga-sutras.md, node 11 section). Not fixed at the time
because it changes the meaning of existing rows.

resolution.note: updateStagedTagConcept dropped from apply.ts and the equivalent concept_id= from review_tags.py; donor keeps its original concept_id with status='reassigned'. Parity preserved (both implementations changed together).
